upstream._note: What the areal append learned about UPSTREAM availability, so the public label can distinguish 'our provider is behind' from 'NLDAS-2 has not published a complete day since X'. The remedies are completely different and the label previously named the wrong one.

served_on: NLDAS-2 basin-average (areal) forcing -- the product it was trained on -- for 95% of the encoder window, with the newest days Open-Meteo point-filled because NLDAS-2 publishes at today-5

superseded.what_it_measured: serving on Open-Meteo point forcing for the WHOLE encoder window, which is what was served before the areal provider landed

_note: The served member now runs on the forcing it was trained on for 95% of its encoder window. The remainder -- the newest days, which NLDAS-2 has not published -- is Open-Meteo point, measured at a paired -0.004018 median NSE (level -0.036142) on val1/150 basins. Quoting the paired figure alone overstates the fix: areal recovers 93.3% of GATE 1's loss paired but only 57.5% on the level. Separately, the 14-day DECODER forcing is a forecast product in every configuration ever measured and neither gate covers it; its closest analogue is the -0.048033 real-forecast decay, a different product on a different frame, which must NOT be added to the above. No figure here is the member's own served skill -- that is still unmeasured, and scripts/score_m1_live.py is what will measure it.
